rationale: All 17 blocking findings from code-review-final.json are resolved and confirmed in the source at HEAD: the four criticals (--agent no longer diverting a TTY invocation into headless, the marketplace scope now merged into the headless assistant catalog, fetchSkillsByIds now throwing on an unavailable id, and skill readability pre-flighted before the first write) plus all thirteen majors, including the cross-scope config copy, the unrecorded partial writes, the duplicate id/slug last-wins pick, the headless re-auth prompt, and the three test-coverage gaps. The three deliberate deviations are accepted: CR-001 bounded the round-trip cost with per_page 100 and documented why minimal_response must stay false (those rows are the registration payload), CR-003 took the recommendation's second option and rejects --project/--all-projects up front, and CR-012 kept spec-mandated case-insensitive matching while removing the silent last-wins. No spec non-goal was breached - no rollback, telemetry, --json, schema change or auto-detected target was added, and the three unrelated known defects are untouched.

business_review.item: Approach: non-interactive branch added to setupAssistants and setupSkills via headless flags on existing commands; no new verb
business_review.notes: Branches at assistants/setup/index.ts:74-76 and skills/setup/index.ts:108-110; flags added on the existing factories; no new command file.

business_review.item: Approach: headless when any headless flag or -y is present, or when process.stdin.isTTY is not true
business_review.notes: isHeadlessMode (shared/headless.ts:22-28) short-circuits on non-TTY then ORs the flags; both call sites pass process.stdin.isTTY === true.

business_review.item: Approach: headless inputs explicit, never inferred — --scope, --agent and (assistants) --mode required; auto-detection never runs
business_review.notes: requireFlag/parseScopeFlag/parseRegistrationModeFlag validate up front; headless uses parseAgentSetupTarget, not resolveAgentSetupTargets.

business_review.item: Approach: multi-value flags are comma-separated, matching the existing --agent <agents>
business_review.notes: parseListFlag splits, trims and de-dupes on comma (shared/headless.ts:63-71).

business_review.item: Approach: identifiers resolve by id, slug, or exact name, case-insensitively; a name matching several is an ambiguity error, never a pick
business_review.notes: resolveIdentifiers covers all three, but duplicate ids/slugs silently last-wins (CR-012) and the skills catalog carries no slug, so slug resolution is unreachable for skills.

business_review.item: Approach: fail-fast is one contract for both modes — pre-flight resolves every identifier and confirms every target before the first filesystem write
business_review.notes: Assistants side fixed (fetchAssistantsByIds propagates, RegistrationItemNotFoundError, executeWithSpinnerStrict), but the skills wizard still drops unavailable ids (CR-015) and skills pre-flight is inside the write loop (CR-016).

business_review.item: Approach: atomicity stops at pre-flight — a failure after writing begins aborts and reports which items were already written, with no rollback
business_review.notes: registerAllOrAbort writes sequentially and throws PartialRegistrationError carrying the written names; no rollback code added, per spec.

business_review.item: Approach: the skills notice is informational — headless prints the same text and continues; the interactive Enter gate is unchanged
business_review.notes: printSkillsNotice uses console.log with no stdin read; showDisclaimer untouched.

business_review.item: Approach: both wiring sites gain the flags together (cli/commands/setup.ts and agents/core/AgentCLI.ts)
business_review.notes: Both sites call the same factories (setup.ts:27-28, AgentCLI.ts:115-116), so flags declared inside them reach both surfaces.

business_review.item: AC: a single non-interactive command registers several assistants and/or skills with no prompt and no raw-mode call
business_review.notes: Happy path is prompt-free, but getAuthenticatedClient can still reach promptReauthentication whose only guard is !process.stdin.isTTY (CR-017).

business_review.item: AC: a requested item not available to the authenticated user aborts the entire run with a named, actionable error and a non-zero exit, in both modes
business_review.notes: Holds headlessly and in the assistants wizard; the skills wizard still filters unknown ids out silently (CR-015). Marketplace assistants also produce a false unavailability error (CR-002).

business_review.item: AC: the abort happens before any artifact is written under .claude/.codex/.gemini and before config is saved
business_review.notes: Identifier resolution and auth precede the writes, but fetchSkillById runs inside the registerAllOrAbort callback, so a per-skill failure aborts after earlier items were written (CR-016).

business_review.item: AC: authentication is verified before any side effect
business_review.notes: getAuthenticatedClient runs before the catalog fetch and every write in both headless branches; flag validation rejects earlier still. Only console output precedes it.

business_review.item: AC: missing --scope, --agent, or assistant registration mode in headless mode each fail with an error naming the missing flag
business_review.notes: requireFlag throws ConfigurationError('Missing required flag: <flag>'); invalid --mode/--scope are also named. Asserted per flag in both headless test files.

business_review.item: AC: an identifier matching no item, and a name matching several, produce distinct typed errors
business_review.notes: RegistrationItemNotFoundError vs AmbiguousIdentifierError, both new CodeMieError subclasses; covered by shared/__tests__/identifier-resolution.test.ts.

business_review.item: AC: a mid-write failure aborts and reports the already-written items by name
business_review.notes: PartialRegistrationError lists written names plus the cause message, surfaced by handleSetupError; covered by registration-writes.test.ts. Config-record consequence tracked as CR-011.

business_review.item: AC: with no headless flags at a TTY, wizard behaviour — search, panels, re-registration — is unchanged
business_review.notes: isHeadlessMode treats the pre-existing --agent (and --scope/--mode) as headless triggers, so `setup assistants --agent claude` at a TTY now errors instead of running the wizard (CR-009).

business_review.item: AC: both `codemie setup ...` and `codemie-<agent> setup ...` expose the same flags
business_review.notes: Flags are identical because both wiring sites share the factories, but the per-agent surface cannot use them without repeating --agent since hostAgent is ignored headlessly (CR-005).

business_review.item: Non-goal: do not rebuild, restyle, or replace the interactive selection wizard
business_review.notes: No selection/ or ui.ts files in the diff.

business_review.item: Non-goal: do not change the `codemie skills add|update|remove|list|find` upstream-wrapper surface
business_review.notes: skills/add.ts and the wrapper commands are absent from the diff.

business_review.item: Non-goal: no telemetry for the new path; SkillCommand unchanged
business_review.notes: skills-metrics.ts not in the diff; no metrics calls added in either headless branch.

business_review.item: Non-goal: no machine-readable (--json) registration output
business_review.notes: Only --assistant/--skill/--scope/--mode/-y added; headless output is the same chalk summary.

business_review.item: Non-goal: no config schema changes or migration — records still append to codemieAssistants / codemieSkills
business_review.notes: Headless saves via the existing save helpers with the same record shapes; env/types.ts not in the diff. Scope-mixing defect is CR-006, not a schema change.

business_review.item: Non-goal: no filesystem rollback of artifacts written before an abort
business_review.notes: registerAllOrAbort documents and implements stop-at-first-failure with no unwind (shared/helpers.ts:77-96).

business_review.item: Non-goal: no auto-detecting agent targets in headless mode
business_review.notes: Headless uses parseAgentSetupTarget on a required --agent; resolveAgentSetupTargets asserted uncalled in both headless tests.

business_review.item: Non-goal: leave unrelated known defects alone (hostAgent dropped on back-navigation, loadSkillsByScope .claude-only, registerSkill slug mismatch)
business_review.notes: Back-nav `return setupAssistants(options)` still drops hostAgent; utils/config.ts absent from diff; skills helpers change is only the null-return removal.

business_review.item: Non-goal: no backfilling coverage for untested orchestration beyond what the new paths require
business_review.notes: New test files cover only headless branches, identifier resolution and the strict write helpers. Gaps in the new paths themselves are CR-007, CR-008, CR-013.

standards_review.notes: 7 subjects in 086875eb..HEAD all match git-workflow.md <type>(<scope>): <subject>; types feat/fix and scope cli are both in the documented enums, subjects are imperative and well under subject-max-length; branch feat/codemie-assistant-skill-registration matches feat/<kebab-description>

Met on imports (.js extensions, import type, no require), explicit return types on every new export, kebab-case filenames, interface-over-type, const/async-await, no debug console.log, files under 500 lines; two documented rules unmet: JSDoc omitted from the new public executeWithSpinnerStrict, and 'functions under 50 lines' exceeded by both headless entry points

Resolved .ai-run/guides/security/security-practices.md. No attribution-header surface touched; no hardcoded secrets; new logger.debug calls carry only CLI flag values and no credential-bearing fields; --scope parsed strictly to global|local, identifiers resolved against the server catalog and never used to build paths, filename derivation stays behind sanitizeToSlug

finding_status.notes: fetchAllPagesForScope now pages at ALL_VISIBLE_PER_PAGE = 100 (assistants/setup/data.ts:55,209), cutting the crawl from ceil(N/5) to ceil(N/100) round-trips. minimal_response deliberately left false with a documented reason: these rows are the registration payload handed to writeOneAssistant/getFullAssistant, so a minimal row would lack generator fields. Accepted - the round-trip cost the finding priced is what the fix removes.

fetchAllVisibleAssistants now pages API_SCOPE.VISIBLE_TO_USER and API_SCOPE.MARKETPLACE and merges de-duplicated by id (data.ts:227-247), with marketplace carrying filters.marketplace = null to match the wizard panel. A marketplace assistant named via --assistant now resolves instead of raising RegistrationItemNotFoundError.

parseHeadlessAssistantFlags rejects --project/--all-projects up front with a ConfigurationError naming --assistant as the explicit alternative (assistants/setup/index.ts:204-209), before auth and any fetch. This is the recommendation's second option; the flag is no longer silently inert. Covered by the 'rejects --project/--all-projects before authenticating' case.

setupAssistantsHeadless is now 45 lines (index.ts:226-270) and setupSkillsHeadless 47 lines (skills/setup/index.ts:302-348), both under the documented 50. The flag prologue is extracted to parseHeadlessAssistantFlags/parseHeadlessSkillFlags and the additive-scoping split to partitionRegisteredByRequest in shared/headless.ts, which is also now directly testable.

New resolveHeadlessAgentTarget(value, hostAgent) (shared/headless.ts:97-102) falls back to hostAgent and only requireFlag-fails when both are absent; both headless flag parsers call it. codemie-claude setup assistants --assistant X --scope global --mode agent now works. Both headless suites assert the hosting-agent path registers for it.

The headless assistants branch loads ConfigLoader.loadAssistantsByScope(storageScope, workingDir) (index.ts:237) instead of the cross-scope loadRegisteredAssistants, so untouchedRegistered/carryOver only contains entries already in the scope being written. Pinned by the 'reads only the scope it writes' test.

assistants headless suite adds 'registers in skill mode and persists registrationMode: skill' (headless.test.ts:324-341), asserting registerAssistant receives 'skill' and the saved entry carries registrationMode: 'skill' - exactly the requested assertion pair.

Both headless suites add 'records the assistants/skills already written when a later write in the batch fails': the second of three registers rejects, PartialRegistrationError is asserted, and the save is asserted to have been called with the first item (assistants headless.test.ts:343-374, skills headless.test.ts:319-346). This drives the real command entry point, not just registerAllOrAbort.

isHeadlessMode now triggers only on flags.yes/assistant/skill (shared/headless.ts:38-44); --agent, --scope and --mode are documented as wizard preselectors in both the HeadlessFlags interface and the function doc, which also now correctly says stdin rather than stdout. MESSAGES.SETUP.OPTION_YES reads 'Run non-interactively; requires --assistant, --scope, --mode and --agent' (assistants/constants.ts:62) and the skills equivalent matches. Both suites assert the wizard still runs at a TTY with --agent alone.
executeWithSpinnerStrict carries a JSDoc block stating it rethrows after onError, in explicit contrast to executeWithSpinner returning null (shared/helpers.ts:39-45).

New persistPartialWrites (shared/helpers.ts:111-125) is called from the catch in applyChangesAndSave (assistants index.ts:325-328), registerAndSaveSkills (skills index.ts:223-226) and setupSkillsHeadless (skills index.ts:344-347), saving untouched + written before rethrowing, with a swallowed save failure so it cannot mask the registration error. The re-register unregister is now per item immediately before its replacement write (writeOneAssistant index.ts:410-412, writeOneSkill skills index.ts:446-448) rather than up front for the batch, so an earlier failure no longer leaves a working registration deleted and unwritten.

resolveIdentifiers buckets id, slug and name alike via bucket() and throws AmbiguousIdentifierError whenever any bucket holds more than one entry (identifier-resolution.ts:41-72). Case-insensitivity is retained deliberately - the spec mandates case-insensitive identifiers - and the doc-comment now states that entries differing only in case collide, which was the other half of the recommendation. Accepted: the silent last-wins pick the finding was about is gone.

Both headless suites add 'passes every --agent target through to the writers and persists them' with agent: 'codex,gemini', asserting registerAssistant/registerSkill receive ['codex','gemini'] and the persisted record carries those agentTargets (assistants headless.test.ts:305-321, skills headless.test.ts:273-288).

New buildScopeFilters is shared by the wizard fetch and the headless crawl, and fetchAllVisibleSkills pages exactly the wizard's two scopes ('project', 'marketplace') with those filters, merged de-duplicated by id (skills/setup/data.ts:28-37,144-185). The unfiltered listPaginated call and its unobservable server-side default are gone, so the reachability question the finding was capped for no longer arises.

fetchSkillsByIds resolves each requested id against the catalog and throws RegistrationItemNotFoundError for any id it cannot find (skills/setup/data.ts:201-209) instead of filtering silently, so the interactive wizard now aborts on an unavailable skill like the assistants path.

New prefetchSkillDetails fetches every skill's detail up front and both paths abort before the first write and before any unregister: interactive at skills/setup/index.ts:166 and headless via applySkillChanges at index.ts:406, with writes taking the pre-fetched detail through requireSkillDetail. The 'proves every skill is readable before the first artifact is written' test asserts registerSkill, unregisterSkill and the save are all uncalled when the third detail fetch 403s.

getAuthenticatedClient takes an AuthenticationOptions { nonInteractive } and skips promptReauthentication when set (utils/auth.ts:15-23,62), and both headless branches pass { nonInteractive: true } (assistants index.ts:234, skills index.ts:312), so a flag-triggered headless run at a TTY fails fast instead of prompting. Asserted in both suites.
